name: Umleqwa
summary: Hardbody (free-range) chicken simmered slowly until tender, then browned in its own fat and finished in a rich onion and tomato gravy.
about: Umleqwa is the isiXhosa name for a free-range “hardbody” chicken; the word comes from chasing, because the birds run when you try to catch them. Tougher than a supermarket bird, it is cooked long and slow, and in many isiXhosa and isiZulu homes it is the Sunday and celebration chicken, served with samp, pap or dombolo.

ingredients.name: Hardbody chicken
ingredients.note: free-range or village chicken, cut into portions

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil
ingredients.note: only if the pot is dry

steps: Rinse the chicken portions and put them in a heavy pot with the water, salt and bay leaves. Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 1 hour, turning the pieces now and then. (A supermarket chicken needs only 20 minutes here.)
Take off the lid, turn the heat to medium and let the water boil away completely, 20–30 minutes, until the chicken starts to sizzle in its own fat.
Fry the pieces in that fat, turning them, until browned all over, 5–8 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil only if the pot is dry and catching.
Add the onions and cook, stirring, until soft and golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, curry powder and paprika and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the tomatoes and the stock and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Cover and simmer on low for 45–60 minutes, adding a splash of water if it starts to catch, until the meat comes away from the bone and the gravy is thick and glossy.
Season with the pepper and taste for salt. Serve hot with pap, samp or dombolo and steamed cabbage.
prepNote: It tastes even better the next day; reheat gently with a splash of water.
